newsitem.title: USA: Teleport to buy CERFnet Internet firm.
newsitem.headline: Teleport to buy CERFnet Internet firm.

text.p: Teleport Communications Group Inc (TCG) on Monday said it would buy Internet service provider CERFnet from General Atomics and its affiliates in exchange for 2.1 million class 'A' common shares.
TCG is majority owned by a group of cable TV firms. Its 'A' class stock closed at $31.625 on Friday, giving an approximate value of $66.4 million for the deal.
General Atomics is a founding participant in the National Science Foundation Network, which later evolved into the Internet.
CERFnet, based in San Diego, is one of the oldest Internet providers, having been set up in 1989. It has 6,000 mainly corporate and professional users.
Teleport predicted CERFnet would generate revenues of $9.3 million for fiscal 1996 and earnings before interest taxes, depreciation and amortization of $1.8 million.

"TCG will provide CERFnet's customer base with sophisticated telecommunication services, while CERFnet will provide TCG's customer base with equally high-quality Internet service," Teleport chief executive Robert Annunziata said.

Staten Island, NY-based Teleport Communications is 31.1 percent owned by Tele-Communications Inc , 24.4 percent by Cox Communications Inc, 16.0 percent by Comcast Corp and 11.0 percent by U S West Media Group's Continental Cablevison Inc.

Annunziata last week told Reuters he was looking for acquisitions either in Internet services or long distance calling to keep Teleport's growth on track and provide the best mix of high-value services to a demanding market place.
CERfnet is a "Tier 1" Internet service provider which puts it near the core of the loose global network of computer systems by providing access to the network for other Internet service providers.

Analysts say Internet service is one of the most attractive added-value propositions for acquisitive telephone companies. It saves the Internet company money it might have spent on upgrading networks, and gives the phone firm access to a group of active, high spending customers.

MFS Communications Co Inc's takeover of Internet company UUnet in 1996 was of this type, and the combined company was attractive enough to be taken over almost immediately afterwards for $14 billion by WorldCom Inc.
